ISSUE:
Changelog drops merge commits

Our release branches are merged with merge commits whose subjects carry the pull request titles, for example `Merge pull request #41 from team/export`, and the generated changelog never lists them.

`CommitsCmd("v1.2.0", "HEAD")` builds:

    git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD

Expected:

    git log --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD

so merge subjects become part of the changelog.

Preferred fix: stop passing `--no-merges` when listing the commits for the changelog. Filtering a second query afterwards would also work, but it doubles the git calls.

=== TASK 1 ===
ISSUE:
#2257 Completions modify os.Args

I'm trying to workaround https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1877 by inspecting `os.Args` by hand. In some cases cobra accidentally inserts `--` into `os.Args`.

Minimal example:
```go
package main

import (
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func main() {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		TraverseChildren: true,
		ValidArgsFunction: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]cobra.Completion, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
			cobra.CompErrorln(strings.Join(os.Args[1:], ", "))
			return nil, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveDefault
		},
	}
	if err := cmd.Execute(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

```

Expected behaviour:
```console
$ go run . __complete x
[Debug] [Error] __complete, x
:0
Completion ended with directive: ShellCompDirectiveDefault
```

Actual behaviour:
```console
$ go run . __complete x
[Debug] [Error] __complete, --
:0
Completion ended with directive: ShellCompDirectiveDefault
```

=== TASK 2 ===
ISSUE:
si: don't give infinities and NaN an SI prefix

ComputeSI clamps the exponent to the range siPrefixTable can name. For an
infinite input the exponent is +Inf, so the clamp pins it to 30 and the
value comes back labelled "Q": SI(math.Inf(1), "x") returns "+Inf Qx",
as if it were a finite number scaled by 10^30. (Before the clamp, the
same input divided Inf by Inf and came back as "NaN x".)

Return non-finite inputs unchanged with no prefix, as ComputeSI already
does for zero, so SI(math.Inf(1), "x") is "+Inf x".
